title: Make a great product: why a great product pushes itself
summary: Levels reflects on self-releasing his 2008 drum & bass album, building and marketing everything himself. He concludes that marketing can take you far, but time is better spent making the product great, and that gatekeepers and tastemakers still matter.

principles.text: A truly great product pushes itself; invest in quality before marketing.
principles.quote: Make a great product. Chances are it will push itself before you even thought about marketing it.

principles.text: Time spent on promotion is often better spent making the product better.
principles.quote: if I had dedicated the time I spent on marketing and promoting it on making the music better I think it would have gone much further.

principles.text: You can market a product to success but cannot force people to like it.
principles.quote: you can market your music to success but you can not force people to like your music.

principles.text: You cannot do everything alone; you need tastemakers and respected people to push your name.
principles.quote: you cannot do everything on your own. And even if you can, you don’t want to. You are always going to need others

principles.text: Get really good first and don't self-release too early; significant people find good work.
principles.quote: don’t release your own stuff independently too early. Get really good at making music first.

principles.text: Self-marketing gets you far, but an absolutely great product pushes itself.
principles.quote: Marketing your product and putting it to the market yourself can get you far, but an absolutely great product pushes itself.
